builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: UnifiedPlayers: Enhance Tool-Integrated Reasoning in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: UnifiedPlayers replaces static verifiers and self-consistency reward signals in self-evolving tool-integrated reasoning with three jointly trained players (task planner, trajectory executor, executable-verifier constructor) coordinated under GRPO. It costs a full reinforcement learning pipeline training three interacting model roles on model backbones, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU budget and adds substantial engineering complexity around reward design and co-adaptation stability. It can fail through coordination instability, where each player's updates shift the data and feedback distribution of the others, and through verifier reward hacking if the evaluation player is exploited by the executor.
rationale: The method requires training multiple cooperating players with GRPO rather than an inference-time technique, so it demands training infrastructure and tuning effort that a constrained team cannot justify until distilled or lighter variants appear.
technique: Cooperative multi-player RL for self-evolving tool-use agents

claims.statement: UnifiedPlayers replaces static verifiers and self-consistency reward signals in self-evolving tool-integrated reasoning with three jointly trained players (task planner, trajectory executor, executable-verifier constructor) coordinated under GRPO. It costs a full reinforcement learning pipeline training three interacting model roles on model backbones, which exceeds a single 24 GB GPU budget and adds substantial engineering complexity around reward design and co-adaptation stability. It can fail through coordination instability, where each player's updates shift the data and feedback distribution of the others, and through verifier reward hacking if the evaluation player is exploited by the executor.

Outperforms the strongest prior baseline by at least 3.5 percentage points on mathematical reasoning and 3.9 points on general reasoning across twelve benchmarks; learned verifier reaches 84.2% adversarial detection accuracy with 2.03x higher per-question reward variance than self-consistency.
